brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb: a centre hex base with six surrounding hex bases
requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases (piece) at axial (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1), all level 0, touching in a flower.

requirements.requirement: Standing on at least three stud spikes
requirements.evidence: Six stud spikes (spike, variant stud) placed at the outer junctions of the honeycomb, each where three cells meet, at level 0.
All six spikes were added with facing 'down' in the addSpike ops; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb (centre plus six around) on one level, with six stud spikes facing down at junctions around the perimeter as feet. Closed open faces with solid caps and locked joints with joint bolts per house rules. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear. No props were added since the brief concerns only the structure.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
